chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:

If the muhrim slaughters game, neither the halal person nor the muhrim may eat it, and it is like carrion. And if game is slaughtered in the Haram, then it is carrion, whether one in a halal state slaughtered it or one in a haram state.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary where special prohibitions apply
key_terms.الْحَلَالُ: a person not in the state of ihram
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: carrion, an animal treated as unlawfully dead and not lawful to eat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on game slaughtered by a muhrim or slaughtered within the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning hunted game in the state of ihram and within the sacred precinct. Game slaughtered by a muhrim is not lawful to eat for anyone, and game slaughtered within the Haram is treated as carrion regardless of who slaughtered it.
